summary: 48 holdings; the top ten are 57% of the portfolio.
Trades moderately: about 29% of the portfolio changes in a year.
The average holding, by value, has been owned for at least 8.0 years.
Compared with the typical S&P 500 company, its holdings are more expensive, more profitable, faster-growing and much larger.
Copying each filing beat the S&P 500 in 2 of 9 full years.

profile.background: Carleton College (1970). After a decade as an analyst and portfolio manager in Omaha, founded Wallace R. Weitz & Company there in 1983. A Berkshire Hathaway shareholder for more than 35 years.
profile.approach: Values a business like an owner, as the present value of its future cash, and favours good management and capital allocation; increasingly willing to pay more for higher-quality businesses.
known: Reported to have returned about 14% a year over three decades, against 11% for the S&P 500.
